rules.title: EPA FIFRA Antimicrobial / Pesticide Registration Trigger
rules.expected_requirement: EPA FIFRA Registration Number & Establishment Number required for antimicrobial claims on inanimate surfaces.
rules.explanation: Under 40 CFR § 152.15, products claiming to kill, inhibit, or eliminate microorganisms on inanimate surfaces are classified as pesticides/antimicrobials under FIFRA. Selling without EPA registration causes immediate US customs seizure and marketplace delisting.
rules.fix_suggestion: Remove antimicrobial/germ-killing claims or rephrase to 'cleans surfaces naturally' without pesticidal or pathogen eradication claims.

rules.title: FDA Unapproved New Drug Claim Prohibition
rules.expected_requirement: Cosmetic and dietary supplement claims must be restricted to structure/function support, not disease treatment or cure.
rules.explanation: Claiming to 'cure', 'treat', or 'prevent' a disease or medical condition legally reclassifies a cosmetic or herbal supplement into an unapproved new drug under Section 505 of the FD&C Act, triggering FDA warning letters and import detention without physical examination (DWPE).
rules.fix_suggestion: Replace disease claims with compliant structure/function language: replace 'cures arthritis / eliminates pain' with 'formulated to support joint comfort and soothe tired muscles'.

rules.title: Hydrogen Peroxide Direct-to-Consumer Threshold
rules.expected_requirement: Maximum 14.0% w/w for OTC consumer whitening products; must include specific safety warnings.
rules.explanation: US FDA permits OTC teeth whitening products containing up to 14% hydrogen peroxide, but concentrations above this threshold are restricted to professional dental use.
rules.fix_suggestion: Ensure hydrogen peroxide content does not exceed 14.0% for US consumer distribution.

rules.title: Camphor Concentration Limit for Topical Analgesics
rules.expected_requirement: Maximum 11.0% camphor concentration in topical consumer products.
rules.explanation: Topical preparations containing greater than 11% camphor are considered misbranded and dangerous to public health due to seizure and toxicity risks under 21 CFR § 310.545.
rules.fix_suggestion: Reformulate product to ensure camphor content is under 11.0%.

rules.title: US Customs Mandatory Country of Origin Marking
rules.expected_requirement: Every article of foreign origin imported into the US must be marked with the English name of the country of origin.
rules.explanation: Section 304 of the Tariff Act of 1930 requires clear marking in English ('Made in [Country]' or 'Product of [Country]'). Failure leads to a 10% marking duty or CBP rejection at the port of entry.
rules.fix_suggestion: Explicitly declare 'Made in [Country of Origin]' on product packaging and listing description.

rules.statute_citation: 16 CFR § 500.6 / Fair Packaging and Labeling Act (FPLA)
rules.title: Net Quantity Dual Unit Declaration (US Customary & Metric)
rules.expected_requirement: Net quantity must be declared in both US Customary units (fl oz, oz, lb) and Metric units (ml, g).
rules.explanation: FPLA mandates dual declaration for consumer packaged goods sold across US interstate commerce.
rules.fix_suggestion: Add dual net quantity declaration, e.g., 'Net Wt. 3.4 oz (100 g)' or '3.38 fl oz (100 ml)'.

rules.statute_citation: Safe Sleep for Babies Act of 2021 (H.R. 3182) / 16 CFR Part 1236
rules.title: Infant Sleep Positioner and Inclined Sleeper Ban
rules.expected_requirement: Total federal ban on inclined sleepers (>10 degrees) and infant sleep positioners in the United States.
rules.explanation: The Safe Sleep for Babies Act banned all infant sleep positioners regardless of marketing claims due to documented suffocation hazards. Violations trigger immediate CPSC recall and federal enforcement.
rules.fix_suggestion: This product category cannot be sold in the United States. Do not list in the US market.

rules.title: CPSC Safety Standard for Infant Walkers (Certification Escalation)
rules.expected_requirement: Children's Product Certificate (CPC) issued by a CPSC-accepted 3rd-party testing laboratory verifying ASTM F977 stair-fall test compliance.
rules.explanation: Baby walkers ARE legal in the US, but MUST possess a valid Children's Product Certificate (CPC) and undergo stair-fall friction testing. This requires laboratory documentation that cannot be auto-resolved by listing text.
rules.fix_suggestion: Obtain accredited CPSC 3rd-party lab test report and issue Children's Product Certificate (CPC) prior to shipping.

rules.statute_citation: 49 CFR § 173.185 / UN Manual of Tests and Criteria Section 38.3
rules.title: Lithium Battery Hazardous Materials Transport Standard
rules.expected_requirement: UN 38.3 Lithium Battery Test Summary, Watt-hour rating <= 100 Wh, and UN3481 package handling label.
rules.explanation: Rechargeable lithium battery devices are Class 9 Dangerous Goods. Cross-border air freight requires verified UN 38.3 test summaries from the cell manufacturer.
rules.fix_suggestion: Obtain UN 38.3 Test Summary report from battery supplier and apply IATA Lithium Battery Mark.
